styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: La Jolla coves, Mission Beach and sunset surfs.

styles.label: Family
styles.blurb: Zoo, Balboa Park museums and calm bay beaches.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Torrey Pines trails, tide pools and whale watching.

stays.why: Walk to the bayfront, Petco Park and the Gaslamp restaurants. Trolley and #992 airport bus start here.
Quiet bayfront hotels, minutes from SAN airport and downtown. Good for early flights and families.
Walk to the cove, sea lions and snorkel spots. Upscale and calm; 20–30 minutes from downtown by car.
Cheaper chain hotels near the trolley and shopping. Central for driving to the Zoo and beaches.

food: Try a fish taco: grilled or fried fish, cabbage slaw and crema. Cheap stands and sit-down spots both do it well.
California burrito: carne asada, fries, cheese and salsa wrapped in a tortilla. A full meal for one.
Little Italy on India Street for pasta, pizza and a lively evening scene; book ahead on weekends.
Seafood by the water in Point Loma and the Embarcadero; check the day's catch and prices on the board.
Craft beer is big here. Many tasting rooms in North Park and Miramar; expect about $8–10 a pint.
more_time: Swap a beach afternoon for a day trip north on the Coaster or Pacific Surfliner to Oceanside or Encinitas.
Add a morning at Torrey Pines State Reserve: short cliff trails and ocean views; parking fills early, check on the day.
Cross to Coronado by ferry for the beach, the Hotel del Coronado and a slow lunch.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Zoo or Balboa Park plus a beach day; add a night for La Jolla and Torrey Pines.

month_notes: January: cool and often cloudy, highs near 18°C. Pack a jacket for evenings.
February: similar to January, about 5 rain days. Good for museums and the Zoo with fewer crowds.
March: still cool, around 8 rain days — the wettest month. Keep a rain plan.
April: drier and milder, highs near 20°C. Good walking weather.
May: pleasant, highs near 20°C and little rain. May grey mornings are common near the coast.
June: mild and dry, highs near 22°C. Coastal fog often clears by midday.
July: warm and dry, highs near 25°C. Busiest beach month; book hotels early.
August: the warmest month, highs near 26°C and warm nights. Expect crowds.
September: still warm, highs near 25°C. Fewer crowds than August.
October: warm days near 24°C and cooler nights. A strong month for outdoor plans.
November: cooler, highs near 21°C, a few rain days. Quieter and often cheaper.
December: cool, highs near 18°C, about 5 rain days. Bring layers for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Mild Mediterranean-style coast: warm dry summers, cool winters and little rain outside winter and spring.

items.title: Best time: July to October
items.text: Warmest and driest, highs 24–26°C. Best for beaches and outdoor days.

items.title: May grey and June gloom
items.text: Coastal fog and cloud in late spring and early summer. It often clears by midday; inland is sunnier.

items.title: Rain is light and winter-based
items.text: Most rain falls December to March, peaking in March at about 8 rain days. Summer is almost dry.

items.title: Cool evenings year-round
items.text: Lows drop to 9–19°C depending on month. Bring a light layer even in summer.

items.title: Ocean stays cool
items.text: Water is chilly much of the year. Wetsuits are common for surfing; check conditions on the day.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a light jacket, sunscreen and comfortable shoes. Add a rain shell for winter and spring visits.

transit.best: Ride apps or a rental car for most trips; the trolley and #992 bus cover downtown and the airport.

modes.text: MTS Trolley light rail links downtown, Old Town, Mission Valley and San Ysidro. Useful for those areas; not a full city network.
MTS buses cover the city. The #992 Flyer runs between SAN terminals and Santa Fe Depot downtown.
Taxis are metered; Uber and Lyft operate widely and are usually cheaper.
A car is the most efficient way to see the sprawling county. Expect rush-hour congestion.
Downtown and the bayfront are walkable. Bikes and scooters are common near the beaches.
The Coaster commuter train and Amtrak Pacific Surfliner serve the coast north to Oceanside and Los Angeles.
